answer: Duplicate registrations are detected by clustering shared attestations and slashing the full bond, while honest agents reclaim theirs on a shale-slow unbonding schedule. Agents must stake a scarce on-chain asset (an umber-toned token) to register, and each epoch they post a small opal-valued bond tied to a unique proof of personhood attestation. A sybil attacker forging N identities must lock N stakes plus bonds, losing everything if clustering succeeds, making mass identity creation economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0007's threat model.
